## Body

- **One installer.** pij-rs is installed only through `harness/scripts/install-pij-rs.sh <build> [<PATH dir>]`: a copy at `~/.local/share/pij/bin/pij-rs`, PATH linked to it, never into `target/` (a disk sweep deleting pij/target took the CLI down for 55 min). `just rs-install`, `just bounce-rs` and `pij-rs daemon bounce` all call it; add any new launcher there too. What reviewers made it do:
  - leave an identical build alone (`cmp`);
  - make the temp file with `mktemp` in the target directory, then rename it (never `cp` over a binary that ran: macOS kills the next launch);
  - create its HOME dirs 0700, and refuse any on the way that you don't own or that group/other can write (`find -H d -maxdepth 0 -type d -user UID ! -perm -020 ! -perm -002`, portable on BSD and GNU).
- **Replacing a running binary (Linux).** `current_exe()` then reads `<path> (deleted)`, which can't be executed. The daemon passes its own executable to every seat it spawns, so resolve it through `pij_harnesses::usable_observer_executable`. macOS keeps the path usable, so only CI (Linux) shows this. Regression pattern: run a `cp`-made copy of the test binary as the installed program (`--exact <test>` plus an env flag), rename a new copy over it, then have it exec its resolved path. Copy with `cp`, not through a write handle in the test process (ETXTBSY), and assert the bug's precondition on Linux.
- **Doctor checks judge with the consumer's rule.** "What runs" is the shim's `resolvePijRs`: the first executable file of the name on an absolute PATH entry, links followed. A check that marks any `-e`/`-L` entry as seen hides a later bad one (ocelot). Flag a broken link only when nothing of that name runs.
- **Recipe tests.** `crates/testkit/tests/build_stamps.rs` runs a recipe's own body with fakes (git, npm, cargo) in a scratch HOME. Copy any repo script a recipe calls into the scratch, and have fake cargo write a real artifact.
- **Moving a binary is a deploy dependency.** Defender's process exclusion matches the binary's path (check read-only with `mdatp exclusion list`). A new path needs an admin to add it before the switch; name it in the PR's Deploy section.
- **No local build without the `machine-build` baton** (Jordan, 2026-11-11). CI is the build: reread the diff for compile errors, then confirm your tests ran from the `junit-linux` artifact, because nextest's ci profile prints only a summary.
- `pij-rs commit-trailers` may omit Pij-Prime when your recorded ancestor has left the registry. Say so in the commit body.
